entities.name: optimization flywheel
entities.description: the loop of resetting the database, re-ingesting data with new parameters, re-evaluating, and comparing on the metrics of choice

entities.name: judge refinement cycle
entities.description: The cycle of build, measure, diagnose disagreements, adjust, and repeat until alignment is sufficient.

entities.name: Terminal-Bench
entities.description: a benchmark that applies hidden oracle tests to terminal tasks, used to compare agents' performance against others

entities.name: prompt caching
entities.description: reuse of a shared prefix across calls, which does not help when every document has a different prefix

entities.name: data fragmentation
entities.description: the situation where data lives in silos across documents, notes, research, emails and text messages instead of a single database

entities.name: LLM
entities.description: the model an agent uses to decide dynamically what to do next

entities.name: SWE-bench
entities.description: a benchmark that applies the hidden oracle test pattern to real GitHub issues

entities.name: subtypes
entities.description: optional extensions of the five base POLE+O nouns, added where the generic types clash with real data

entities.name: information silos
entities.description: a failure mode created by splitting tightly coupled tasks across multiple decision makers

entities.name: five-component architecture
entities.description: the five-component system that turns raw documents into queryable memory

entities.name: overengineering
entities.description: building solutions more complex than needed, such as multi-agent architectures where a simple workflow would be faster to build, cheaper to run and easier to debug

entities.name: tool calling
entities.description: The request-execute-respond flow where an LLM names a tool and arguments, your code runs it and returns the output to the LLM

entities.name: linting
entities.description: the constant sweep of the wiki for orphan sources, broken links, stale claims, and contradictions

entities.name: gap analysis
entities.description: a between-rounds step that flags thin or missing themes against the initial key themes

entities.name: precision
entities.description: the fraction of judge-approved traces that the expert also labeled Pass, calculated as TP / (TP + FP)

entities.name: Polymorphism
entities.description: Lets the application layer interact with an interface such as BaseLLM instead of a hard-coded concrete class, so implementations can be swapped through configuration

entities.name: continual learning
entities.description: a process in which what the agent learns flows back into the memory

entities.name: multi-modal ingestion
entities.description: Embedding the image and the surrounding caption into two separate collections, one keyed on image vectors and one on caption text vectors.

entities.name: context isolation
entities.description: the central design choice that every step touching real source content runs in an isolated subagent with its own context window

entities.name: labeled property graph
entities.description: a graph model that attaches metadata as JSON on the entity or relationship, used in practice by GraphRAG and agents

entities.name: Prompt Chaining
entities.description: a pattern that connects multiple LLM calls or other processing steps sequentially, where the output of one step becomes the input for the next

entities.name: lost in the middle
entities.description: an issue where the model ignores information in long contexts

entities.name: relevance score
entities.description: a score between 0.0 and 1.0 given to every candidate, with seed URIs always getting 1.0

entities.name: deduplication
entities.description: the step that decides whether a new node gets created at all

entities.name: few-shot prompt
entities.description: the prompt holding the train-set examples that set the standard for what Pass and Fail look like

entities.name: class imbalance
entities.description: a skew where one class dominates the traces, such as 90% Pass and only 10% Fail

entities.name: feedback loops
entities.description: The loop the evaluator-optimizer pattern creates to automatically improve and refine the output of an LLM.

entities.name: Clean Architecture
entities.description: Pattern that organizes a system into four concentric layers whose dependencies point inward

entities.name: pragmatic clean architecture design
entities.description: A loose, tool- and framework-agnostic version of Clean Architecture applied to AI engineering that keeps only the principles making code modular, flexible, testable and maintainable

entities.name: Routing
entities.description: a pattern that directs the workflow down different paths based on the input or an intermediate state, like a smart if-else statement where an LLM acts as a classifier

entities.name: DDD glossary
entities.description: a shared vocabulary between business and engineering at docs/glossary.md that enforces one canonical name per concept

entities.name: nested relationships
entities.description: a storage design that duplicates edges and makes them awkward to query

entities.name: tool selection
entities.description: the agent's choice of the right tool, which gets harder and degrades as the tool list grows past roughly 10 to 20 tools

entities.name: PARA method
entities.description: a method of organizing everything into Projects, Areas, Resources, and Archive

entities.name: full-screen
entities.description: A TUI approach that takes over the terminal's viewport as a grid of cells, giving total layout control but losing scrollback and search.

entities.name: vibe coding
entities.description: prompting an agent to produce code that compiles and looks done but breaks the moment you reach for the rough edges

entities.name: text search
entities.description: search that uses exact keywords

entities.name: reasoning LLMs
entities.description: LLMs with a "thinking" feature that reasons in an internal trace managed by the API, separate from the final output

entities.name: accuracy
entities.description: the overall agreement rate between judge and expert, calculated as (TP + TN) / total

entities.name: context stuffing
entities.description: Putting everything into the model's context window, which degrades performance.

entities.name: Parallelization
entities.description: a pattern that runs as many steps as possible concurrently, as long as they do not depend on each other's outputs

entities.name: append-only log
entities.description: a data model of an immutable log of every event plus a queryable materialized view, which never deletes or updates and gives versioning and temporality

entities.name: single knowledge graph collection
entities.description: the simple design that keeps the whole knowledge graph in one MongoDB collection

entities.name: cross-encoder
entities.description: a heavier model that compares the query against each candidate

entities.name: golden links
entities.description: a few hand-picked links given to the loop up front as seed context

entities.name: tool count problem
entities.description: the problem that tool selection degrades once a single agent has more than roughly 10 to 20 tools

entities.name: lineage
entities.description: the references kept on each knowledge-graph node to the documents it was extracted from, the user who owns it and other metadata

entities.name: parallel execution with majority voting
entities.description: a workflow pattern that runs tasks in parallel and aggregates the answers by majority voting

entities.name: bounded context
entities.description: one directory per business module, with each domain owning its own types, store, API and prompts

entities.name: observability
entities.description: First-class observability implemented with Opik, baked in from the first commit.

entities.name: agentic GraphRAG
entities.description: GraphRAG where an agent autonomously writes to and searches the knowledge graph

entities.name: structured outputs
entities.description: the practice of forcing an LLM's response into a predictable format such as JSON or a Pydantic model, acting as a formal contract between the LLM and application code

entities.name: graph search
entities.description: a multi-hop traversal across the typed edges

entities.name: one-shot
entities.description: having an agent build a feature in one go; the author says it works for scoped big features but not whole applications

entities.name: versioning
entities.description: What an append-only log plus a materialized view buys for free, and the reason to reach for the log.

entities.name: Architecture Decision Record
entities.description: a record of a non-obvious choice with its status, context, decision and consequences, kept at docs/adr

entities.name: domain layer
entities.description: Innermost layer holding business objects (Entities) and units of AI work (Nodes), unaware of databases, APIs or LLMs

entities.name: planning
entities.description: the separation of the reasoning process from the action of calling tools, the step that turns a workflow into an agent

entities.name: file-system state tracking
entities.description: A technique Claude Code and OpenAI Codex rely on instead of true RLM patterns, alongside summarization-based context compression and progressive disclosure.

entities.name: read actions
entities.description: Tools that gather information into the agent's context window, such as real-time APIs and database queries

entities.name: harness engineering
entities.description: the work around the agent loop such as memory, compaction, skills, the permission layer and sandboxes

entities.name: reserved GPU time
entities.description: reserving GPUs for the peak and paying for it for the entire length of the contract

entities.name: non-determinism
entities.description: the randomness from the judge producing different scores on the same input and from the agent taking different paths each run

entities.name: Text-to-SQL
entities.description: Tools that translate natural language questions into SQL or NoSQL queries to retrieve data from structured databases

entities.name: hallucination
entities.description: A potential failure mode in which the agent might hallucinate an answer.

entities.name: knowledge graph
entities.description: a store of knowledge as entities and typed edges that maps naturally to an agent's unified memory

entities.name: top-down GraphRAG
entities.description: the GraphRAG variant that hops across communities for a high-level overview

entities.name: frontier model
entities.description: The strongest available model, like the latest versions of Claude Opus or Gemini Pro, used for the judge because it should be at least as capable as the system it evaluates.

entities.name: API rate limits
entities.description: limits, known as Requests Per Minute quotas, that LLM APIs impose and that must be managed in a production application

entities.name: semi-structured extraction
entities.description: extraction that uses metadata and lineage without an LLM, such as parsing an email's links and attachments

entities.name: doom loop
entities.description: a failure mode where the agent gets stuck looping and burns tokens

entities.name: NL query
entities.description: agentic search that lets the LLM write its own MongoDB queries based on the ontology

entities.name: Plan-and-Execute
entities.description: an action and planning technique that agents often use

entities.name: multi-hop traversal
entities.description: a traversal across the typed edges of the graph, GraphRAG's addition over RAG

entities.name: LongBench-v2 CodeQA
entities.description: A benchmark of codebase question answering on which the RLM paper tested RLMs.

entities.name: context engineering
entities.description: Carefully curating what goes into the context window through retrieval and compression.

entities.name: maximum iteration limit
entities.description: A safeguard a production-ready implementation would include to handle failing agents.

entities.name: Orchestrator-Worker
entities.description: a pattern where a central LLM, the orchestrator, dynamically breaks a complex task into sub-tasks and delegates them to specialized workers that can run in parallel

entities.name: fuzzy matching
entities.description: A resolution strategy that uses RapidFuzz string similarity for surface variants, also used with vector similarity for deduplication.

entities.name: POLE+O
entities.description: a closed five-type vocabulary of Person, Object, Location, Event, and Organization, borrowed from intelligence-analysis taxonomies

entities.name: exploratory extraction
entities.description: extraction that is great early on when figuring out what ontology makes sense for your data

entities.name: Facts
entities.description: the generic fallback entity that holds one atomic subject-predicate-object triplet for knowledge that does not fit a noun or a Preference

entities.name: complexity spectrum
entities.description: a slider from the most control to the most autonomy, with three levels, used to choose between workflows, single agents and multi-agent systems

entities.name: append-to-scrollback
entities.description: A TUI approach that writes like an ordinary CLI, used by Claude Code, Codex, Pi and Decode.

entities.name: semantic search
entities.description: meaning-based search

entities.name: scientific method
entities.description: the experiment-driven approach to finding the best model and configuration for a use case: configure parameters, run experiments, compute metrics, analyze results and pick the best configuration

entities.name: rubric
entities.description: The judge's grading criteria, informed by the train set, which might lack specificity and should be sharpened.

entities.name: dependency injection
entities.description: The injection process that connects the application's abstract needs with the infrastructure's concrete tools, done by the builders.

entities.name: sandboxing
entities.description: Running agent-written code in an isolated environment, required because code execution brings arbitrary code execution and resource exhaustion risks.

entities.name: top-K
entities.description: a retrieval parameter that is free to change and often provides the biggest wins

entities.name: AI evals dataset
entities.description: a dataset defined in YAML with the query, expected answer, expected citations and a minimum relevance score, anchored in real user behavior

entities.name: context rot
entities.description: the mechanism by which LLM performance measurably degrades as context grows, well before hitting the advertised limit

entities.name: confusion matrix
entities.description: a table of four outcomes (TP, TN, FP, FN) from comparing judge verdicts against expert labels

entities.name: traces
entities.description: What you monitor when developing AI agents in production, to debug and analyze the point of failure when planning goes sideways.

entities.name: embedding model
entities.description: What the memory folder approach does without, giving lower costs than a RAG pipeline.

entities.name: Recursive Language Models
entities.description: An inference-time pattern that treats the input as an external environment the model interacts with programmatically by writing code, instead of feeding it into the context window.

entities.name: single-agent architecture
entities.description: an architecture where one agent reasons about a problem and then acts autonomously to solve it

entities.name: AI Evals
entities.description: checks that track and improve the performance of an AI product

entities.name: deep search
entities.description: a retrieval that widens the walk to 3 hops and persists the result to disk as a memory wiki the agent can access via progressive disclosure

entities.name: Test-Driven Development
entities.description: write the failing test, write the minimal code to pass it, then refactor

entities.name: autonomy slider
entities.description: a spectrum between fully controlled workflows and fully autonomous agents, used to decide how much autonomy to grant an AI system

entities.name: pass^k
entities.description: a reliability metric that tracks whether all k attempts succeed

entities.name: community detection
entities.description: a step run after materialization that computes communities over the canonical node collection

entities.name: binary classifier
entities.description: a model that outputs one of two labels, such as Pass or Fail

entities.name: unstructured extraction
entities.description: extraction that uses an LLM without a schema, so the LLM invents its own labels; useful for discovery, not for grounded retrieval

entities.name: autonomous loop
entities.description: the loop where the results from the tools are fed back into the LLM, which decides to call more tools or generate the final answer

entities.name: SAME_AS pattern
entities.description: the three-zone pattern that stops the same entity from becoming three nodes

entities.name: hybrid retrieval
entities.description: retrieval over a hybrid index of text search, semantic search and graph search, joined by Reciprocal Rank Fusion

entities.name: human gates
entities.description: checkpoints in the /night pipeline where the human validates, such as approving the plan

entities.name: experiment
entities.description: An experiment is a single parameterized run over an agent, dataset, embedding, chunking strategy, database, and judge.

entities.name: divide-and-conquer
entities.description: a principle of breaking a large problem into smaller, focused sub-tasks so that each LLM call has a clearer, more constrained objective

entities.name: Map-Reduce
entities.description: a strategy from data engineering where multiple jobs run in parallel while the results are aggregated at the end

entities.name: infinite loop
entities.description: A failure mode in which the agent gets stuck retrying the same failed search.

entities.name: horizontal scaling
entities.description: scaling to millions of documents by adding more clusters

entities.name: compaction
entities.description: a behavior of the harness that keeps the context window small by squashing old interactions into a summary once a threshold is passed

entities.name: write actions
entities.description: Tools that affect the external world, such as executing code or sending emails, riskier because often irreversible

entities.name: benchmark
entities.description: a structured set of experiments in which most variables are held constant to isolate the effect of one

entities.name: separate edge docs
entities.description: a storage design that gives queryable edges, no duplication and the cheapest footprint, at the cost of built-in temporal history and versioning

entities.name: speed-versus-accuracy ladder
entities.description: an extraction design where cheap models take high-confidence cases and only ambiguous mentions escalate to zero-shot models and then an LLM

entities.name: structured extraction
entities.description: schema-guided extraction where the LLM outputs entities per the Person Ontology

entities.name: agentic templates
entities.description: good practices encoded as skills and CLAUDE.md files in markdown instead of frozen code templates, with tooling kept dynamic

entities.name: steering
entities.description: input mode where plain Enter injects the message within a model turn, between tool calls

entities.name: materialized view
entities.description: the queryable collection of canonical records built from the append-only log

entities.name: parallelism
entities.description: the running of genuinely independent tasks simultaneously, one legitimate reason to go multi-agent

entities.name: data validation
entities.description: What structured outputs and Pydantic add, so that bad data raises a clear error instead of propagating.

entities.name: TerminalBench 2.0
entities.description: benchmark on which Pi's minimal tool set ranks in the top 10

entities.name: parallel attempts
entities.description: independent agents implementing the same feature, of which only the best is forwarded for review

entities.name: one-shot LLM calls
entities.description: A single, large LLM call for a complex task, which makes pinpointing errors difficult, lacks modularity and increases lost-in-the-middle issues.

entities.name: Dependency Rule
entities.description: Rule that dependencies must always point inward, so the application and domain layers never know about the infrastructure and serving layers

entities.name: production evals
entities.description: the evals that answer whether the agent keeps working, tracing every session and scoring sampled traces live

entities.name: code execution
entities.description: A write-action tool category where a Python or JavaScript interpreter lets an agent write and run code in a sandboxed environment.

entities.name: ontology
entities.description: a collection of classes and the relationships allowed between them

entities.name: lock-in
entities.description: the loss of context, skills and billing control that comes from building deep into a single harness

entities.name: retry caps
entities.description: limits on loop attempts, such as 5 for the engineer and tester loop and 3 for the acceptance and PR review loops

entities.name: agentic coding
entities.description: using agents to write the whole codebase while the human stays the mastermind behind everything

entities.name: concept confusion
entities.description: a failure mode where, as data grows, the LLM merges how two tools handle something into one explanation

entities.name: resolution
entities.description: the step that sets a canonical string property on an existing reference

entities.name: evaluator validation
entities.description: the process of comparing judge verdicts against expert labels with classification metrics to check that an evaluator's verdicts are correct

entities.name: bottom-up GraphRAG
entities.description: the GraphRAG variant that expands entities for depth

entities.name: LLM extraction
entities.description: a write-path stage where the LLM receives a chunk and returns JSON with nodes and edges

entities.name: pay-per-token
entities.description: Paying per token, which quickly becomes inefficient at high volume compared to paying for compute.

entities.name: checkpointing
entities.description: persisting ingestion state so that a failed run resumes instead of recomputing everything from scratch

entities.name: progressive disclosure
entities.description: the pattern, also used inside skills, that lets an agent choose from many options without drowning in information

entities.name: cooperative abort
entities.description: input mode where Esc sets a flag that stops the turn at the next boundary and clears both queues

entities.name: context overload
entities.description: a condition where instructions and tools degrade an agent's performance, one legitimate reason to go multi-agent

entities.name: false merge
entities.description: an entity merge error that is silent and unrecoverable without re-ingesting from the raw source data

entities.name: normalization
entities.description: the memory pipeline step that tracks the evolution of a single entity over time by re-using the same canonical ID across extractions

entities.name: overkill trap
entities.description: designing the perfect, complete ontology upfront, which freezes the project

entities.name: train/dev/test split
entities.description: the partition of labeled data into train (60%), dev (20%) and test (20%) sets so the judge is not built and validated on the same examples

entities.name: serverless computing
entities.description: paying for the compute actually used instead of tokens or a reserved peak, with the meter following the demand curve

entities.name: regex parsing
entities.description: the fragile approach of parsing LLM responses with regex patterns, which broke in production when response formats varied

entities.name: follow-up
entities.description: input mode where Alt+Enter holds the message until the turn stops and then runs it as one more step

entities.name: false split
entities.description: an entity split error that is noisy but recoverable

entities.name: regression testing
entities.description: the tests that answer whether the agent still works, comparing scores against the baseline on every new feature

entities.name: Global Ontology
entities.description: the digital twin's ontology of six entity types, split into a Document Ontology and a Person Ontology

entities.name: summarization-based context compression
entities.description: A context-handling technique used by Claude Code, Cursor and Codex that loses critical information.

entities.name: infinite optimization loop
entities.description: The main failure mode of the evaluator-optimizer pattern, prevented by clear stop conditions.

entities.name: golden dataset
entities.description: the expert-labeled dataset the LLM judge's verdicts are measured against

entities.name: significance threshold
entities.description: A threshold computed by running the evaluation 3-5 times and computing the variance between the runs, separating noise from real metric shifts.

entities.name: tool calls
entities.description: the output of an orchestrator LLM that names a tool with its arguments, which workers run in parallel

entities.name: few-shot examples
entities.description: labeled train-set examples that go into the judge's prompt and translate to input tokens and extra costs

entities.name: replay
entities.description: re-running a finished run with one thing changed, such as a different model or a fixed prompt, against the original as the baseline

entities.name: Actionability
entities.description: Organizing code so everything related to one task, including its class, system prompt and utility methods, lives in one self-contained module

entities.name: code fragility
entities.description: A downside of RLMs where buggy code written by the model makes the entire reasoning chain fail.

entities.name: data-exploration workflow
entities.description: a loop of running an exploration extraction on real data, inspecting clashes with the generic model, and adding or renaming subtypes

entities.name: ReAct
entities.description: an action and planning technique that agents often use

entities.name: chain-of-thought prompting
entities.description: an early attempt at planning through the "think step by step" instruction that couples thinking and execution into a single LLM output

entities.name: Retrieval-Augmented Generation
entities.description: A strategy for bridging the LLM knowledge gap by fetching relevant context, which requires tools

entities.name: materialization
entities.description: a periodic step that squashes all events sharing an ID into one canonical record

entities.name: tool confusion
entities.description: A failure mode where the LLM mixes up tools, avoided by limiting tool count and writing clear distinct descriptions

entities.name: Folder-per-Type
entities.description: Structure with folders like /prompts, /nodes and /chains that scatters the logic of a single feature across all of them

entities.name: single mutable collection
entities.description: a data model where each extraction directly upserts into the queryable collection, dropping the log

entities.name: GraphRAG
entities.description: A knowledge graph query tool that uncovers relationships between entities to help the agent refine its context

entities.name: context window
entities.description: Where retrieved chunks are added, after further compression, to avoid exploding costs.

entities.name: 2-3 hop traversal
entities.description: the second retrieval stage that walks 2-3 hops across the typed edges to expand the result set

entities.name: pass@k
entities.description: a reliability metric that tracks whether at least one out of k attempts succeeds

entities.name: code templates
entities.description: scaffolding projects from frozen templates, which the author calls a maintenance tax because frameworks and tooling go stale

entities.name: system prompt
entities.description: The prompt that instructs the LLM how to use the tools and includes the schemas of all available tools.

entities.name: Reciprocal Rank Fusion
entities.description: a method that merges text and semantic search results, after which a cutoff gives the entry points

entities.name: infrastructure layer
entities.description: Layer with the concrete implementations of external dependencies such as LLM providers, databases and storage

entities.name: superficiality
entities.description: a failure mode where the LLM's answer needs many follow-ups to get right

entities.name: tracing
entities.description: capturing the spans, configs, token counts and tool inputs and outputs of an agent run

entities.name: recall
entities.description: the fraction of the traces the expert labeled Pass that the judge also finds, calculated as TP / (TP + FN)

entities.name: Evaluator-Optimizer
entities.description: a pattern that creates a feedback loop where an evaluator LLM scores the output of a generator LLM and the generator refines it until a quality score or a maximum number of iterations is reached

entities.name: human-in-the-loop
entities.description: a design practice where a human verifies or approves the steps of an AI system

entities.name: plan-execute-validate
entities.description: An orchestration loop where the root controller plans, worker sub-models execute, and the system validates results until FINAL() is called.

entities.name: F1 score
entities.description: an aggregate metric that is the harmonic mean of precision and recall

entities.name: chunking
entities.description: Splitting data into pieces, which RAG infrastructure needs and RLMs remove the need for in simple cases.

entities.name: Preferences
entities.description: an entity family attached to the graph that records what a noun, usually a person, likes or dislikes

entities.name: embedding
entities.description: Something the system does not use, so references stay perfectly traceable.

entities.name: flat hierarchy
entities.description: Keeping modules at the same level and respecting layer boundaries only virtually rather than through folder nesting

entities.name: agent loop
entities.description: a loop in which a single agent plans, executes, and reflects

entities.name: organizing by actionability
entities.description: the correct project-structure pattern: one bounded context per directory that is locally readable and easier for the agent to reason about

entities.name: gemini-1.5-flash
entities.description: model the example research agent is created with

entities.name: gemini-2.5-flash
entities.description: The Gemini model the article's code calls through generate_content to pick and invoke tools

entities.name: GLM-5.2
entities.description: open-source model of 740B parameters deployed via Modal Endpoints

entities.name: gemini-1.5-flash-lite
entities.description: model, run at temperature 0.3, that the create_summary tool calls to write summaries

entities.name: gemini-3.1-flash-lite
entities.description: a closed-API model used for extraction and query translation

entities.name: voyage-3.5
entities.description: a closed-API embedding model run at 1024 dimensions

entities.name: GLiNER
entities.description: a zero-shot named entity recognition model that can run locally without powerful inference hardware

entities.name: GPT OSS 120B
entities.description: 120B model that is larger than Qwen3.6 35B

entities.name: Gemini
entities.description: Google's LLM and API that lets you declare tools directly in the API call with native tool-calling

entities.name: GLiREL
entities.description: a zero-shot extraction model

entities.name: Qwen3.6 35B
